thread:
Dana: quick heads-up — billing graphs don't match sampled traces for a subset of customers. looks like cohort rebucketing in enrichment is changing attribution after ingress sampling.
Omar: that's the classic sample-after-enrich problem. do we have an existing stabilizer token?
Dana: not really. current flow samples based on trace_id % N at ingest, then enrichment recomputes billing_cohort. when cohort changes, sampled set no longer represents cohort mix.
Priya: proposal: emit a short stable key at ingress (sample_key) used both for sample decision and as a join key for cohort mapping emitted by enrich. billing looks up cohort by sample_key.
Omar: agree. minimal header, versioned (v1: base62 token). fallback: if missing, enrichment writes cohort with sample_key_missing=true so billing can treat it as approximate.
Dana: operational concerns: mapping TTL vs billing lookback windows, collision alerts if sample_key maps to multiple cohorts, and proxy/header loss.
Priya: plan: RFC + small spike: implement header in SDKs (default to trace-derived token), enrich emits mapping to kafka, small consumer writes to redis (7d TTL) and to cold store for backfills.
infra-bot: created ticket INF-9981: "ingress sample_key + cohort mapping spike" -> https://go/internal/INF-9981
Omar: sounds good. I'll run a quick entropy test comparing trace-derived vs rand-uuid tokens and report numbers.
Dana: thanks — I'll start the RFC draft with rollout and backfill strategy.
